content.text:
I've submitted index 62 (Bi 0.27, Fe 0.38, V 0.35) as the best composition. It gave a photocurrent of 1.24×10⁻⁵ A, the highest of the three I could measure.

The budget allowed only three merit measurements. I started near BiVO4, a known photoanode, keeping Bi and V roughly equal, and raised the Fe fraction each time:

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | 0.43 / 0.16 / 0.41 | 7.06×10⁻⁶ |
| 57 | 0.30 / 0.35 / 0.35 | 7.96×10⁻⁶ |
| 62 | 0.27 / 0.38 / 0.35 | 1.24×10⁻⁵ |

Photocurrent went up as Fe increased. After the second measurement the Gaussian-process model suggested index 74, but it predicted only about 5×10⁻⁶ A in a lower-Fe region that was doing worse, so I didn't follow it.

Three points can't show whether photocurrent keeps rising at higher Fe or has already peaked, so better compositions may exist that I didn't measure. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present was not checked.
